scope: Audit of HSConfig source-to-runtime lowering on branch codex/no-silent-default-only-closure for Hearthstone semantic cases that can become false runtime claims when guide prose, card text, or static semantics are lowered too aggressively. The evaluated surface area covers start-of-game effects versus mulligan keeps, hero power transforms, deckbuilding modifiers, targeting rules, combo sequencing, Discover and Choose One options, generated cards, Secrets, Locations, weapons, discard, destroy, silence, transform, and Wild deck mechanics.
verified_strengths: HSConfig currently treats `claim_kind` plus the target surface gate as the runtime authority. The operator policy says source truth becomes runtime config only through `claim_kind`, the source contract matrix, and the surface gate; guide importance, archetype value, and effect relevance do not bypass that chain.

The mulligan gate rejects non-hand start-of-game effects even when a claim is shaped as `mulligan_keep`. The live gate returns `start_of_game_effect_does_not_require_opening_hand`, and regression tests cover Darkbishop Benedictus-style hero-power transforms and deckbuilding start effects.

The source contract matrix keeps `hero_power_transform` in a conditional CardID lane, not in the Mulligan lane. This preserves the effect while preventing a hero-power transform enabler from becoming an opening-hand keep unless separate current mulligan evidence says so.

Semantic qualifiers are explicitly diagnostic refinements, not an alternate apply path. Timing, zone scope, target scope, option surface, and state requirements can suppress unsafe lowering without creating a second runtime-write authority.

Static semantics recognizes the risky families requested in this audit, including Discover, weapon, Secret, discard, silence, transform, destroy, Choose One, Location, start-of-game, deckbuilding modifier, even/odd modifier, Highlander modifier, deck-size modifier, start-in-deck requirement, generated random pools, secret timing, and location activation.

Warning-only semantics are represented as report-visible boundaries. Random generated pools, Secret timing, Location activation, Dredge, Tradeable, Titan, Tourist, Imbue, Forge, Excavate, and related future or state-heavy mechanics can be visible without becoming false runtime rows.

Discover and Choose One have dedicated option surfaces but remain identity-gated. The router suppresses unresolved option identities and only allows a card behavior row when the source card and exact option card identity are linked.

Combo lowering is isolated through `combo_sequence` and an explicit combo sequence contract. One-card, vague, missing-card, or otherwise non-emittable sequences are suppressed instead of converted into partial Combo.json rows.

Card behavior routing requires supported blocks or explicit runtime blocks for high-risk actions. Destroy, generic spell targeting, hero power, silence, and transform usage cannot be emitted from keyword recognition alone.

Mechanic support already distinguishes direct, partial, warning-only, and identity-gated direct mechanics. This gives any-deck operation a safe partial-output lane rather than forcing either full runtime proof or complete blockage.

The no-silent-default-only policy is integrated with operator reporting: default-only surfaces are visible quality debt in `operator_summary.json`, `default_only_runtime_surface_details`, `source_to_runtime_explainability.json`, and the surface status ledger, but they are not an apply blocker when the package is technically valid.
correctness_gaps: Start-of-game and deckbuilding effects must never be treated as opening-hand evidence by default. Cards such as Darkbishop Benedictus, Genn Greymane, Baku the Mooneater, Prince Renathal, Highlander payoffs, start-in-deck effects, and future rulebreakers may be strategically required while still providing no proof that the card should be kept in mulligan.

Hero power transforms need timing, identity, and source-card constraints. A transformed Hero Power can be created before the mulligan, by an in-game play, or by repeated Imbue-style upgrades; lowering generic hero power prose as ordinary Hero Power use can claim the wrong timing or wrong power identity.

Deckbuilding modifiers are not equivalent. Odd/even restrictions, no-duplicate conditions, deck-size and starting-health changes, sideboard or band rules, start-in-deck requirements, and current deck-state checks have different evaluation times and should not be collapsed into one permanent runtime fact.

Targeting advice requires exact legality and current state. Phrases such as go face, remove a threat, target a minion, or use this on your own minion do not prove whether the action is a spell target, Battlecry target, weapon attack, Hero Power target, Location activation, or no-target effect, nor whether stealth, Elusive, immunity, board state, or target death changes legality.

Combo semantics need a complete ordered contract. A guide can mention synergy without proving same-turn order, cross-turn setup, mana availability, hand origin, board space, weapon state, death count, discount state, generated resource identity, or target availability.

Discover and Choose One are option-selection mechanics. A preference such as choose burn, take removal, pick value, or choose the left option is not runtime-safe unless the option identity and source card identity are resolved.

Generated cards and random pools must remain separate from the starting deck. Random generation, copies, shuffled cards, transformed entities, and Discover-like options can matter later, but they cannot be treated as guaranteed ordinary deck-card actions without exact identity evidence.

Secrets combine hidden information with delayed triggers. Advice to play, hold, preserve, or sequence a Secret does not prove the opponent action, trigger timing, legal response, or board state needed for deterministic runtime behavior.
Locations are persistent board objects with activation, durability, and cooldown timing. Treating a Location as a one-shot spell loses activation-state, target-state, and repeat-use constraints.

Weapons require equip state, durability, attack timing, replacement behavior, and target legality. Weapon pressure or weapon synergy prose is not enough to claim an unconditional attack or an opening-hand keep.

Discard, destroy, silence, and transform are distinct operations with different zones and persistence. Discard usually mutates hand or deck plans, destroy may create death events, silence removes effects, and transform replaces an entity. Keyword detection alone does not prove the correct runtime block or target.

Wild decks amplify drift risk because they can combine old start-of-game effects, deckbuilding constraints, generated-card pools, Secrets, weapons, sideboard-like mechanics, and modern keywords. The broader pool increases the chance that a true semantic fact has no safe normal-path runtime surface.
default_only_gaps: A card can be semantically recognized but still produce only baseline CardID behavior if no supported surface or exact option identity exists. The ledger must keep that visible as suppressed, warning-only, or default-only rather than implying runtime competence.

Mulligan output can be policy-backed or source-backed, but an effect-only card should not be hidden as a default keep. If a start-of-game enabler is excluded from Mulligan.json, the effect should remain visible in CardID, posture, or diagnostics so the operator sees that suppression was deliberate.

Warning-only mechanics such as secret timing, location activation, generated random pools, Dredge, Tradeable, and future Wild keywords can leave the package technically valid but thin. The operator view must distinguish valid thin output from a missing or silently defaulted runtime surface.

Identity-gated direct mechanics can look supported in aggregate while a specific unresolved Discover or Choose One claim remains non-emittable. Default-only reporting should identify the unresolved option reason, not only the card name.

Generic card-role rows can be meaningful for priority but are weaker than behavior-block rows. Reports should avoid calling a card fully runtime-backed when it only has an in-hand or static-semantics priority row.
slimness_gaps: Creating a new top-level runtime claim kind for every Hearthstone keyword would bloat the contract spine without adding actual VisionAI authority. Timing, zone, target, option, state, and generation details should remain qualifiers unless they require a distinct supported runtime surface.

Named-card exception lists would be fragile. The Darkbishop rule should remain a general start-of-game non-hand suppression rule, not a growing list for Benedictus, Genn, Baku, Renathal, Highlander cards, and future Wild enablers.

Full deterministic models for Discover pools, Choose One sub-options, random generation, Secret trigger timing, Location activation planning, aura math, and all Wild-only mechanics would duplicate game-engine authority while still failing to prove runtime outcomes.

The same semantic decision should not be reimplemented independently in static semantics, qualifier normalization, the source contract matrix, surface gates, builder/router code, and operator reports. Those layers should share policy vocabulary and suppression reasons to avoid drift.

Diagnostic reports should not become alternate apply gates. The source contract audit, mechanic visibility summaries, surface status ledger, and source-to-runtime explainability should explain quality and debt while leaving apply authority in `operator_summary.json`.

Adding exhaustive generated-card or option trees to normal packages would make packages noisy and stale. HSConfig should emit only resolved, source-backed option identities and keep broad pools report-only.
autonomy_gaps: Any-deck operation must keep producing valid packages for technically valid decks even when a mechanic is unsupported, warning-only, or partially modeled. Blocking on full semantic coverage would make Wild decks impractical.

Static card semantics must remain useful without guide prose, but static recognition cannot become runtime authority. Requiring a guide for every card blocks autonomy; auto-emitting from keyword recognition creates false runtime claims.
Policy-backed autonomous mulligan can prevent empty default-only output, but it must stay separate from source-backed claims and must not overwrite exact current keep or discard evidence.

Runtime evidence should remain mandatory for empirical numeric GlobalValues tuning, but not for safe recognition of static semantics, option-gated surfaces, or report-only warnings. Otherwise source-only package generation stalls unnecessarily.

Unsupported future mechanics need a stable warning-only lane. New expansion mechanics, rulebreakers, and Wild-only interactions should not require immediate runtime compiler support before a package can be generated.

Suppression must preserve operator visibility. If a claim is true but not lowerable, the reason should be visible as `requires_exact_option_identity`, `requires_supported_cardid_surface`, `sequence_too_short`, `requires_runtime_evidence`, warning-only, or an equivalent stable reason.
guardrails_to_keep: Keep `claim_kind` as the runtime-routing source of truth; do not infer runtime authority from card importance, guide praise, archetype role, or the word keep outside exact mulligan context.
Keep `start_of_game_effect_does_not_require_opening_hand` suppression for non-hand start-of-game effects and deckbuilding modifiers.
Keep `hero_power_transform` out of the Mulligan surface by default. Preserve it through CardID or deck posture only when the transformed identity and supported runtime block are known.
Keep Discover and Choose One lowering identity-gated. Unresolved option identities should remain suppressed and report-visible.
Keep Combo.json emission behind explicit `combo_sequence` claims and the combo sequence contract. Do not emit one-card, vague, missing-card, or partial sequences.
Keep explicit runtime-block requirements for destroy, generic spell target, hero power, silence, and transform mechanic usage.

Keep warning-only classifications for generated random pools, secret timing, location activation, Dredge, Tradeable, board positioning, and future mechanics that do not have documented normal-path VisionAI blocks.
Keep GlobalValues posture and numeric tuning separate. Numeric tuning should continue to require runtime evidence instead of guide-only prose.
Keep the no-second-gate boundary: diagnostic reports and surface ledgers explain risk, but `operator_summary.json` remains the normal apply authority.
Keep regression tests that assert both halves of each split: unsafe runtime rows are suppressed, while independently supported correct-surface behavior remains available.
recommended_next_design: Preserve the current slim source-contract spine and strengthen it through shared semantic qualifiers, not broad new runtime surfaces. The design stance should be: recognize Hearthstone semantics early, attach timing, zone, target, option, state, generation, and deck-evaluation qualifiers, then emit only when the claim kind, surface gate, identity resolution, and builder/router contract all agree. Everything else should remain report-visible with a stable suppression reason and should not block technically valid any-deck package generation.
